title: Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another v. J.P. International Sports Ltd. & Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Misra, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
date_display: 26 July 2021 (interim order; order-sheet 26.7.2021 to 24.4.2023, writ petition pending)
disposition: Writ petition pending; not finally decided. On the licensee's petition challenging an order of the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum dated 22 March 2021, the Division Bench, recording that the matter required consideration, stayed by interim order dated 26 July 2021 the effect and operation of that order to the extent it directed re-assessment of the demand on the basis of reduced load, till the next date of listing (the interim order being extended thereafter). The first part of the Forum's order, implementing the Committee's report dated 9 November 2015 for the period 27.10.2011 to 23.11.2011, was left untouched. After several adjournments the matter was last listed for 1 May 2023.
headnote: Order-sheet record of a pending writ petition brought by the licensee, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., against an order of the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum dated 22 March 2021 concerning the bill for a period (27 October 2011 to 20 March 2012) during which no meter was installed at the consumer's premises. The billing dispute had been resolved by a Committee under clause 5.7 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (report dated 9 November 2015); the consumer's complaint travelled through the Forum, the Electricity Ombudsman (which remanded on 28 December 2018), a fresh Forum order, a recall for want of notice, and finally the impugned order of 22 March 2021. That order had two parts: the first implemented the Committee's report for 27.10.2011 to 23.11.2011; the second provided that, on the consumer depositing the amount for that period within one month, the consumption for the remaining period would be reassessed on the basis of reduced load. The licensee, aggrieved only by the second part, contended that where supply is made without a meter clause 5.7 is attracted, requiring the bill to be raised on the basis of three months' average consumption after installation of the meter — the basis on which the Committee had already reported — so that there was no justification to further reduce the consumption. Finding that the matter required consideration, the Division Bench (Manoj Misra and Jayant Banerji, JJ.) stayed the second part (reduced-load reassessment) pending final hearing, and did not decide the clause 5.7 question.
facts: In respect of the supply of electricity to the first respondent, J.P. International Sports Ltd., for the period 27 October 2011 to 20 March 2012, a dispute arose over the demand raised by the petitioner-licensee, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. The dispute was resolved by a Committee on the basis of clause 5.7 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and on the report of the Committee dated 9 November 2015 a bill was raised. The first respondent complained to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum in September 2016, praying that the bill for the period 27.10.2011 to 20.03.2012 — when no meter was installed — be corrected under clause 5.7 on the basis of the average of three months' consumption after installation of the meter. The Forum dismissed the complaint; the first respondent appealed to the Electricity Ombudsman, which by order dated 28 December 2018 remanded the matter; the Forum again confirmed its earlier order on 14 June 2019; on a recall application (allowed 5 March 2020 for want of notice after remand) the Forum re-examined the matter and passed the impugned order dated 22 March 2021, whose operative portion had two parts: the first implemented the Committee's report for consumption from 27.10.2011 to 23.11.2011, and the second provided that if the complainant deposited the amount for that period within one month, the consumption for the remaining period would be assessed on reduced load. Aggrieved only by the second part, the licensee filed Writ - C No. 15712 of 2021, contending that supply without a meter attracts clause 5.7 and its three-months-average measure, on which the Committee had already reported, leaving no justification to further reduce the consumption. On 26 July 2021 the Division Bench, finding the matter required consideration, stayed the second part of the Forum's order pending final hearing; the interim order was extended on later dates and the matter, passing through several benches, was last listed for 1 May 2023.

reusable_constructions.construction: Where electricity has been supplied without a meter, clause 5.7 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is attracted and the bill is to be raised on the basis of the average of three months' consumption after installation of the meter; a licensee may contend that, the assessment Committee having reported on that very basis, there is no justification for a forum to further reduce the consumption on 'reduced load'.

At the instance of the licensee, a Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum's direction to reassess a demand on reduced load may be stayed pending final hearing, while the part of the order that merely implements the assessment Committee's report is left to operate.

principle_tags.application: The consumer's billing grievance over an unmetered period was adjudicated through the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Electricity Ombudsman (which remanded on 28.12.2018) before the licensee challenged the Forum's final order of 22.03.2021 in this writ.

The licensee contended that supply given without a meter attracts clause 5.7, requiring the bill to be raised on three months' average consumption after meter installation — the basis on which the Committee had reported — leaving no room for a further reduction on reduced load; recorded as requiring consideration.

The second part of the Forum's order, directing reassessment of the remaining period on reduced load, was stayed pending final hearing at the licensee's instance, while the part implementing the Committee's report was left to operate.
